issues.claim: V11 §3.1 makes each row's readers cell the one list of a table's readers, a read recorded under the StageId of the stage function that reads, "so every table a stage or phase reads names that stage, and T-V11-1 (b) holds it" (V11 l. 898–915); T-V11-1 (b) asserts every recorded (stage, table) pair over the golden fixtures has the stage among the table's compiled `stageReaders`, "0 unlisted stage readers" (V11 l. 4983; J-V11.90, l. 5265). At generation S4, S5b and S6 lay the viaducts, elevated roads and aqueducts before S7 builds a trace's furniture (§4.1, base l. 5715–5718); `Enceinte.thicknessCm`, `walkCm`, `heightCm` are "written by S7" (l. 2263) and "the wall's thickness, height, walk and tower spacing read its class's row (V11's `walls.barriers`)" (l. 8371–8373). Yet §2.7's laws make those stages read the band, wall strips and top: §4.3 *Where it may not go* has every course, "a viaduct's priced in a route's solve among them", search "only the courses those laws admit (law 1 (2)–(6), (9)–(11), read with their terms …)", an aqueduct crossing each wall at its level (l. 6510); the support step keeps a station off "an enceinte's band (`Enceinte.band`, or before S10 has built it the band beside the standing trace, read as these laws' *the band* and *Not yet built* read it)" (l. 2542–2544); *Not yet built* reads "a band's width, a wall's top … before S7 writes them … as the rows that build it will build it" (l. 2769–2775). Every generated aqueduct on a walled town crosses its enceinte at S6, its terminal inside the outermost enceinte (l. 6495; V06 l. 2871; *over the band*, l. 3025–3027). With no stored source named before S7 and S10, a correct build reads row 14 (`walls.barriers`: thicknessFactor, heightFactor, wall, walk; V11 l. 551) and §4.8's section rows under S4, S5b and S6. Row 14's readers are "S3 (9), S5a, S7 …, VS3 …, SKY …, EVO_GROWTH and EVO_FORT …" (V11 l. 939), row 13's (`walls`, §4.8's table) "S3, S5a, S7" (l. 938); the `S5` group does not reach S5b where a row names S5a (l. 917–918). So T-V11-1 (b) records (S6, `walls.barriers`) on a walled CITY or METROPOLIS golden with a generated aqueduct and fails a correct build. Major (a named test fails a correct build); not VF7w-RDR-02's minor grade, since here the design sends the read to the rows with no stored source and the case is the generator's ordinary path on a walled golden. Row 80 lists the walls' stages as readers of the raised way's cells through the same laws (l. 1006); rows 13 and 14 do not list the raised-way stages.

issues.claim: The fourth fix pass wrote the raised road's gate in law 2's order: §7.1 *Raised ways*, "a gate §2.7's laws bar there (law 1, read with its terms; chiefly (5), (10): a shape-locked wall's among them) resolved by those laws, law 2, in its order: (a) the way's crossing of the wall moved to the nearest place they admit its gate, (b) else the way re-routed through the nearest gate of that wall a way of its class may pass, (c) else refused" (base l. 11155–11159), and V09 §4.20.2 (4) the same, naming its key: "the crossing moved, else the way re-routed through the nearest gate of that wall, else refused (…; `bend.raised.wall`)" (V09 l. 3016–3020). Both moves change the user's own stroke, so each is part of its bend line, never a fate (§2.7's laws, law 4, l. 2872), named by §7.1's catch-all `bend.raised.wall` (l. 11354). V09 §4.9's `bend.raised.wall` line cell words the meeting only as "The raised road comes down before the {wall} and passes through its gate." (V09 l. 2102): no form for a crossing moved {m} m along the wall, none for a road gone round to another gate. Minor: VF7x-HND-01's grade (a line form; the geometry is the laws' and no bar counts lines).
issues.required_change: V09 l. 2102, `bend.raised.wall`'s line cell: after ""The raised road comes down before the {wall} and passes through its gate."" insert " — and, where §2.7's laws bar its road's gate there (law 1, read with its terms, chiefly (5), (10); law 2, in its order, law 3; *Carried way*), for the road's crossing of {wall} moved along it, "The raised road comes down before the {wall}; its road crosses the wall {m} m along, where a gate can stand.", and for the road re-routed through a standing gate, "The raised road comes down before the {wall}; its road goes round to {gate}." — `{gate}` the gate's name, else its kind's word".

issues.claim: V04 §3.5.4 (d) (1) glosses a span the laws read `open` under a wall as "— under a wall the arch beneath the band walled up by the run —" (V04 l. 1696–1697). The laws give the run's top beneath a raised way by law 1 (2) and (7): *the cap*, "the lower of its own top and the lowest soffit there … (the soffit lower: the arch walled up to its crown; the run lower: the arch open above it); beneath an aqueduct, over or merged, and beneath a fallen span, a support bearing none or no deck, its own top" (base l. 3094–3100), and law 1 (2)'s over form has "every span above the band clearing the wall's top, the band passing beneath the arch" (l. 2708–2709). Under an aqueduct's over crossing, and under a road deck whose soffit stands above the run's top, the arch is open above the run; the gloss also names "the band" where the wall strips alone may read the span `open` (law 1 (8)'s *anything across a strip*, l. 2644–2645). Minor: no rule, drawing or bar reads the gloss (the chamber rule is "none in a span they read `open`"); a restatement the laws already decide.
issues.required_change: V04 l. 1696–1697: "— under a wall the arch beneath the band walled up by the run —" → "— under a wall its arch open above the run or walled up to its crown by it, as §2.7's laws give the run's top there (law 1 (2), (7); its worked example *the cap* in *beneath*) —".

issues.claim: V11's table-edit pattern (V11 l. 863) resolves by §2.7's laws the meetings each item-110 cell's edit makes — `stripMarginM` ("every meeting the widened strip, zone or ends make with a wall-like structure resolved by §2.7's laws (law 4; law 1 (11), J148; law 2 (a)–(c), by hand the edit refused), never kept against them"), §4.8's band and setback rows and `palisade.bandM` ("as `stripMarginM`'s does"), `deckDepthCm` and the rows that give a wall's top ("re-checks each crossing … by §2.7's laws (law 4; …)"). Its clause for the support step's own bounds says only "a `slideMaxFactor` or `maxClearSpanM` edit re-runs the support step on the generated ways (keys kept by item 244 (5)), a standing way a lowered bound now refuses kept and listed with the remove offer, as the pattern keeps it". The re-run moves and merges stations, so it can bring a ring or a span's strip onto what the laws bar there — a gate's or tower's footprint in the setbacks (law 1 (5): "never on a support's ring"), a held building's span (law 1 (9)) — which law 4 re-checks for "a width, class or table edit" (base l. 2863). Minor: the laws govern and §5.3's row catches a wrong build; a reader of an op path omitting the re-check its sibling clauses name.
issues.required_change: V11 l. 863: "a `slideMaxFactor` or `maxClearSpanM` edit re-runs the support step on the generated ways (keys kept by item 244 (5)), a standing way a lowered bound now refuses kept and listed with the remove offer, as the pattern keeps it;" → "a `slideMaxFactor` or `maxClearSpanM` edit re-runs the support step on the generated ways (keys kept by item 244 (5)), a standing way a lowered bound now refuses kept and listed with the remove offer, as the pattern keeps it — and every meeting a station it moves or a span it merges makes with a wall-like structure or a held building resolved by §2.7's laws (law 4; law 2 (a)–(c), by hand the edit refused), never kept against them, as `stripMarginM`'s does;".
